page: Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a constrained vCPU profile consisting of 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The processor package provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance is allocated 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is included, requiring the use of remote storage volumes, and no dedicated GPU accelerators are attached.

Benchmark results position the E32-16s_v5 in the middle 50% across most standard computational and memory benchmarks. The system delivers a PassMark CPU score of 21320.68 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10064.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth achieves 103.31 GB/sec, while write operations reach 58.66 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, the instance registers 16.01 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations score of 7995.58. For machine learning tasks, the system demonstrates strong relative output on text generation using small 135M parameter models at 321.0 tokens per second, while larger 7B model generation runs at 15.6 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency on the E32-16s_v5 is driven by its high memory-to-core ratio, which enables deployments needing significant RAM without incurring the software licensing or compute costs of a full 32-core allocation. However, the complete lack of local scratch storage necessitates additional remote block storage attachments, introducing latency and operational expense tradeoffs for high-IOPS demands. The server fits in-memory caching systems, intermediate database tiers, data analytics engines, and enterprise software instances constrained primarily by memory capacity rather than compute throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for workloads demanding elevated memory capacity relative to compute allocations. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Architectural features include 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction set support. The instance includes no local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached volumes. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the E32-16s_v5 exhibits balanced median performance, scoring 10064.0 in Geekbench multi-core and maintaining 16.01 million Redis SET operations per second. The constrained core count enables cost savings for software licensing models tied to CPU cores while satisfying substantial RAM footprints, making the instance a practical choice for in-memory databases, large-scale caching, data warehousing, and ETL processing.
